concept.name: Supply zone
concept.definition: A price band marking the base from which a strong decline launched, drawn (in supply-and-demand methodology) around the small consolidation preceding the impulsive drop. It is treated as potential resistance on a return, on the hypothesis that unfilled sell interest remains there — a discretionary zone framework related to, but looser than, classical resistance.
concept.intuition: Price paused, then fell out of bed; the pause zone is where sellers were last in control, so the first return there may meet them again.
concept.mechanics: Identify an impulsive decline; step back to the small base candles just before it. Draw the zone around the base — proximal line at the edge nearest current price, distal line at the base's extreme — and extend it right. Reversal zones (rally-base-drop) form at swing turns; continuation zones (drop-base-drop) form mid-swing.
concept.failure_modes: Zones are re-drawn to fit hindsight, and price trades straight through many of them; continuation-type (RBR/DBD) zones are documented by practitioners as weaker than reversal-type zones.
concept.misconceptions: That a supply zone is proof of institutional sell orders waiting there; the zone marks where price left a base impulsively, and the unfilled-orders story is an inference, not an observation.
concept.example: EUR/USD pauses for three small candles at 1.0850-1.0860, then drops 100 pips; the base is drawn as a supply zone and watched for a short entry on the first return.
